content:
maya: quick check — planning a Terraform change for svc: payment-processor in staging. Goal: set externalTrafficPolicy: Local to preserve client IP and use an NLB with TLS passthrough for port 443. Two asks: (1) any hidden implications for nodePort allocation / pod distribution / healthchecks? (2) TLS termination: should we terminate at Gateway (certs in k8s secret, rotate via KMS) or keep passthrough on NLB and terminate downstream? link to PR: https://git.internal/redwood/infra/pull/412 :eyes:

alex: fyi i'm +1 for externalTrafficPolicy: Local if you need real client IP in logs/ratelimit. watch out though — Local means only nodes with endpoints will accept traffic, so you must ensure pod spread and nodePort range allocation are okay. health checks need to hit nodePort on the node (not pod IP) and target group config must match. sample service snippet we used previously:

```
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: payment-processor
spec:
  type: LoadBalancer
  externalTrafficPolicy: Local
  ports:
  - port: 443
    targetPort: 8443
    protocol: TCP
```

alex: also check `spec.healthCheckPort` in the aws_lb_target_group resource in TF — we point it at the nodePort. failing to update that causes 503s. :warning:

jordan: regarding TLS termination — if you terminate at the Gateway (Gateway API) you get easier routing (SNI-based routes, HTTP routing, auth plugins) and can manage certs as k8s Secrets. But that adds CPU/latency on pods if we re-encrypt downstream. Passthrough at NLB means we keep TLS to the pod and offload certs to the app or sidecar, and rotation is app-level. For audits/regulatory customers we might prefer Gateway termination + KMS-backed secrets. My vote: Gateway termination for staging->prod parity, unless the app requires mTLS to pod.

samir: small TF notes from similar change: when switching LB type / target group attributes we had to update `deregistration_delay` and `slow_start` to avoid connection churn. Also, if you rely on sessionAffinity: ClientIP on the Service, it doesn't play well with externalTrafficPolicy Local + NLB passthrough — session affinity at k8s level is sticky to client IP but NLB passthrough preserves src, so ok, but it can lead to uneven load if pods are uneven. add a pre-change smoke test: deploy 3 pods across 3 nodes, curl from multiple external IPs and check HA/heatmap.

samir: FYI the TF change will touch these resources: `kubernetes_service.payment_processor`, `aws_lb_target_group.payment-tg`, `aws_lb_listener.https`, and `aws_lb_target_group_attachment.*`. plan showed one replace on tg.

deploy-bot: PR 412: terraform plan completed on staging (apply pending approval). Summary: 1 to replace, 2 to update. See plan: https://ci.internal/builds/98312 :white_check_mark:

maya: good context, thanks. action items: @alex can you review health-check port mapping and nodePort policy in the PR? @jordan can you weigh in on Gateway vs passthrough for prod (esp. cert rotation ops)? i'll add the smoke-test matrix to the PR and schedule a quick canary deploy on staging tomorrow morning. target apply window: 03/30 09:00 UTC. tag: @samir for TF rollback steps. :thumbsup:

alex: on it, i'll push a tiny TF change to set `health_check_port = var.node_port` and add a note about nodeSelector spread.

jordan: will write a short doc in the PR comparing termination modes + ops for rotation (KMS/HSM notes). leaning gateway termination but will add exceptions.

maya: thanks — if nothing else by EOD i'll merge and we can coordinate the staging apply tomorrow. any objections speak now, otherwise i'll assign reviewers and merge. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
